smartImport.title: Smart Import
smartImport.description: Paste character profiles, introductions, location descriptions, organization notes, or other fact-oriented setting material. Mimoria will turn recognized information into suggestions for you to review before anything is written to your world.
smartImport.inputHint: Smart Import works best with profile-style and setting-reference text. Dialogue-heavy scenes, everyday interactions, and continuous narrative prose are not currently recommended.
smartImport.placeholder: Example: Alice is a 24-year-old alchemist from Silverport. She is a member of the Black Rose Church.
smartImport.textRequired: Paste some structured world information first.
smartImport.suggestionsDescription: Review each recognized change before applying it to this world's Canon.
smartImport.suggestionsEmpty: No new structured changes were found.

onboarding.clickHighlighted: Click the highlighted area to continue
onboarding.welcomeDescription: Mimoria is currently in Beta development. This short tour will walk you through the basic worldbuilding workflow: creating a world, defining entity types, creating entities, writing documents, and trying Smart Import. You can skip the tour at any time from the top-right corner.
onboarding.createWorldDescription: A world is the container for all of your setting data in Mimoria. Click the highlighted New World button to begin.
onboarding.tutorialWorldDescription: A temporary tutorial world used to learn the basic Mimoria worldbuilding workflow.
onboarding.confirmWorldDescription: We've filled in a sample world for you. Click the highlighted Create World button to complete your first world creation.
onboarding.entityTypesDescription: Entity Types define what fields characters, locations, items, and other world data can contain. Click the highlighted Entity Types section to continue.
onboarding.createEntityTypeDescription: Entity Types work like templates for your world data. Characters, locations, organizations, and other information can each have different fields. Click New Entity Type to begin.
onboarding.tutorialEntityTypeDescription: Used to store people and characters in this world.
onboarding.entityTypeNameDescription: The name identifies this type throughout Mimoria. We've prepared “Character” for the tutorial.
onboarding.entityTypeIconDescription: Icons help you quickly distinguish different types. Mimoria supports Emoji icons, so we'll use 👤 here.
onboarding.entityTypeDescriptionDescription: The description explains what this type is intended to store. It does not restrict the fields themselves.
onboarding.confirmEntityTypeDescription: The name, icon, and description are ready. Click the highlighted Create Entity Type button to finish.
onboarding.openEntityTypeDescription: The Character type is ready. Click the highlighted card so we can define its fields next.
onboarding.fieldsOverviewDescription: Each Entity Type can have its own fields. Name is a built-in Mimoria field. Next, we'll create a custom field.
onboarding.addFieldDescription: Click Add Field. We'll add a simple Age field to the Character type.
onboarding.fieldNameDescription: The field name describes the information being stored. We've prepared Age for the tutorial.
onboarding.fieldTypeDescription: The field type determines how the value is entered and stored. Age works well as a Number.
onboarding.fieldRequiredDescription: Required fields must be filled when an entity is created. We'll leave Age optional for now.
onboarding.confirmFieldDescription: The field is ready. Click the highlighted Add Field button to save it.
onboarding.fieldCreatedDescription: Every Character entity can now store an Age value. Entity forms automatically follow the fields defined here.
onboarding.entitiesNextDescription: Entities are the actual characters, places, items, and other records in your world. Click the highlighted Entities section to continue.
onboarding.entitiesOverviewDescription: Entities are the actual characters, locations, items, and other records in your world. Their forms follow the Entity Types you define.
onboarding.createEntityDescription: Click New Entity. We'll create an example using the Character type you just made.
onboarding.entityTypeSelectionDescription: The Entity Type determines which fields this entity has. The tutorial has already selected your Character type.
onboarding.entityNameDescription: Every entity has a name. We've prepared Aerin as the example character.
onboarding.entityCustomFieldDescription: Remember the Age field you created? It now appears automatically in the Character form. We've entered 24 for Aerin.
onboarding.confirmCreateEntityDescription: The example character is ready. Click the highlighted Create button to save the entity.
onboarding.entityDetailDescription: After creation, Mimoria shows the entity's details here. Every field defined by its Entity Type can be displayed here.
onboarding.editEntityDescription: Click Edit to see how saved information can be changed.
onboarding.editEntityFieldDescription: Fields defined by the Entity Type automatically become editing controls. You can change Age or any other stored information.
onboarding.saveEntityEditDescription: Click Save Changes. Future edits work the same way.
onboarding.secondaryWorkspaceDescription: On wide display mode, Mimoria can show two workspaces at once. You can keep Entities open while viewing Documents, Entity Types, or other information beside them.
onboarding.workspaceSplitterDescription: Drag the divider between the two workspaces to control how much space each side uses.
onboarding.dockHandleDescription: Dockable items in the left navigation have a drag handle. Drag from this handle when you want to open a workspace without leaving the current one.
onboarding.dockingAreaDescription: Drop a dockable workspace here to open it in the secondary workspace. You can also switch its contents from the selector at the top of the secondary pane.
onboarding.documentsNextDescription: Documents are for chapters, story writing, world history, and other long-form content. Click the highlighted Documents section to continue.
onboarding.documentsOverviewDescription: Documents are useful for longer worldbuilding notes, story drafts, and other free-form writing.
onboarding.documentsTreeDescription: The explorer on the left organizes your documents. You can use folders and drag items to rearrange their order and hierarchy.
onboarding.createDocumentDescription: Click New Document to create a simple tutorial document.
onboarding.documentTitleDescription: The title identifies this document in the explorer. We have prepared an example title for you.
onboarding.confirmDocumentDescription: Click the highlighted Create button to finish creating this document.
onboarding.documentCreatedTitle: Your Document Is in the Explorer
onboarding.documentCreatedDescription: The document you just created now appears in the explorer. You can use this area to open and organize documents later.
onboarding.documentEditorDescription: This is Mimoria's rich-text editor. Use it for lore, stories, notes, and other longer pieces of writing.
onboarding.documentToolbarDescription: The toolbar provides bold, italic, headings, lists, quotes, undo, redo, and other common formatting tools.
onboarding.documentContentDescription: Click inside the editor and type a little text. When you're ready, click Next to continue.
onboarding.documentAutoSaveDescription: Mimoria automatically saves the document shortly after you stop typing. You can check the current save state here.
onboarding.entityAddedToTreeDescription: The entity you just created now appears in the explorer on the left. New entities will also be added here automatically.
onboarding.entityTreeDescription: The explorer on the left organizes your entities. You can create folders, drag entities to rearrange them, and organize the information in your world.
onboarding.smartImportNavDescription: Finally, let's see how Mimoria can turn existing setting notes into structured suggestions. Click Smart Import to continue.
onboarding.smartImportOverviewDescription: Smart Import can recognize characters, locations, organizations, and field information from existing setting notes and turn them into reviewable suggestions.
onboarding.smartImportUsageTitle: Use Setting Notes, Not Narrative Prose
onboarding.smartImportUsageDescription: Smart Import works best with character profiles, character introductions, location descriptions, organization notes, and other direct descriptions of facts. It is not currently designed for dialogue-heavy scenes, everyday interactions, or continuous narrative prose where facts depend heavily on context.
onboarding.smartImportInputDescription: Enter existing setting material here. The tutorial has prepared a short character profile as an example.
onboarding.smartImportExampleText: Eileen is a 23-year-old alchemist from the North. She is quiet and cautious, and is currently a member of the Silver Moon Association.
onboarding.smartImportAnalyzeDescription: Run the analysis. Mimoria will try to turn facts in the text into structured suggestions, but it will not immediately change your world.
onboarding.smartImportSummaryDescription: This summary shows how many suggestions are waiting for review and how much information already matches the existing Canon.
onboarding.smartImportSuggestionsDescription: Recognized information appears as suggestions first. Review the entities, fields, and values before deciding whether to apply them.
onboarding.smartImportApplyTitle: You Decide What Enters the World
onboarding.smartImportApplyDescription: A suggestion only changes the world after you click Apply. If the result is incorrect, you can edit or ignore it instead.
onboarding.smartImportErrorDescription: Smart Import may not always interpret natural language perfectly. Here, part of “Eileen is 23 years old” was incorrectly recognized as an entity name. This is why Mimoria creates suggestions first instead of changing your database automatically.
onboarding.smartImportEditDescription: If an extracted name, field, or relationship is incorrect, you can fix it before applying the suggestion. Click Edit Suggestion to continue.
onboarding.smartImportEditNameDescription: The recognized entity name is incorrect. Change it to “Eileen”, then continue.
onboarding.smartImportSaveEditDescription: Saving updates the suggestion with your corrected information, but it still does not write anything into the world yet.
onboarding.smartImportIgnoreDescription: If a recognized suggestion is not useful, you can ignore it. Ignoring a suggestion does not change any existing world data.
onboarding.smartImportRecommendedTypeDescription: Mimoria recommends an Entity Type based on the recognized content and tries to reuse an existing matching type whenever possible.
onboarding.smartImportManualTypeTitle: You Can Choose a Type Manually
onboarding.smartImportManualTypeDescription: If the recommended type does not fit your world, you can manually select another existing Entity Type here.
